description: Ready-to-use, ultra quick-drying, flexible liquid membrane for waterproofing interior and exterior surfaces
whereToUse: Waterproofing before applying ceramic, stone, and mosaic coverings
saunas and damp environments in general
notFor: Do not apply Mapelastic AquaDefense if the temperature is lower than +5°C.
Mapelastic AquaDefense must always be covered with ceramic, mosaic or stone.
Do not apply Mapelastic AquaDefense on cementitious substrates with residual humidity higher than 3% or subject to recurring rising damp.
Do not apply Mapelastic AquaDefense on crumbly cementitious substrates, old floors that are not well bonded to the substrate or surface treatments which could affect the bond.
Do not use Mapelastic AquaDefense to cover cracks.

standards.value: Product certified according to EN 14891, waterproofing under tile

technicalData.label: Waiting time before application of the covering
Complete drying of 1 mm thick layer
Impermeability to water under pressure (EN 14891-A.7) (1500 kPa)
Mapelastic AquaDefense must be applied in
technicalData.value: two thin (approx. 0.4 mm per coat), even coats

packaging: 3.5 kg, 7.5 kg, and 15 kg rectangular bucket.
storage: Mapelastic AquaDefense can be stored for 24 months in its original packaging in a dry area. Protect from frost.
notes: The only consumption figure is 1 kg/m² for 2 coats; it is not split by roller, brush or trowel and no per-coat or per-mm figure is given. The sheet requires two coats at approx. 0.4 mm per coat but states no minimum total thickness as such; the FINAL PERFORMANCE table is headed '0.55 mm thickness' and the drying row refers to a '1 mm thick layer', so three different thicknesses appear. Waiting time before tiling is given two ways: table '3-4 hours', body text 'can be laid 4 hours after the application of the second coat'. 'Solid content: 66' is printed without a unit. The EN 14891 certification is stated without a class designation. Minimum filming temperature is +5°C and the recommended application range is +5°C to +35°C. If Mapetex 50 fabric is embedded the sheet says drying times may increase and the final thickness increases, with no consumption figure for that case. No mixing ratio exists (ready-to-use, one-component), so mixing is null. The WHERE TO USE section also lists substrates (concrete; cementitious screeds; plasterboard, for application in interior only; old ceramic tiles, terrazzo, and stone material; cementitious render), not included in whereToUse. One table column header is left in Italian in the sheet ('Requisiti secondo EN 14891').
